articles.originalTitle: planted roof connects concrete casa cieno by TAC to oaxacan coast - Designboom
articles.title: TAC Taller Alberto Calleja Completes Diagonally Oriented Concrete House in Puerto Escondido
articles.excerpt: Located on the Oaxacan coast in Mexico, Casa Cieno turns inward rather than facing the sea, organizing its program around a central pool and vegetated courtyards.
articles.content: Constructed in Puerto Escondido, Mexico, Casa Cieno was designed by TAC Taller Alberto Calleja on a 1,500 square meter plot. The main volume of the residence is positioned diagonally in relation to the property boundaries, creating green buffer zones between the building and neighboring properties. Serving as the primary visual and spatial anchor, a central pool anchors a layout organized around enclosed courtyards and framed views. The design team separated the social and private areas through the water element, with pathways crossing the pool to connect to two bedrooms. A circular opening in the roof slab frames the sky above the pool, introducing natural light into the interior. The material palette combines exposed concrete and wood, selected in response to the climatic conditions of the Oaxacan coast and intended to age with the site. A green roof extends the living space above, restoring part of the displaced vegetation while contributing to the residence's natural climate control.

articles.originalTitle: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition - ArchDaily
articles.title: Designing the Climate Transition: Between Catastrophe Scenarios and Technological Utopias
articles.excerpt: While climate change discussions frequently focus on apocalyptic scenarios or technological salvation, the crucial, gradual work of multi-decade repair, adaptation, and maintenance remains largely underappreciated in design narratives.
articles.content: While cinematic and literary narratives frequently explore climate failure, technological transformations and smart cities offer optimized resource management and new urban futures. Projects such as The Line at NEOM propose entirely new urban conditions independent of existing physical constraints, offering a clean slate for future living. However, the climate transition will rely less on a single breakthrough and more on decades of parallel work streams involving adaptation, maintenance, repair, and resilience. Ordinary interventions—such as retrofitting buildings, gradually shifting energy systems, and restoring landscapes—constitute the cumulative foundation of systemic change. The primary challenge for designers and storytellers lies in visualizing and bringing this slow, distributed middle ground of transformation into the collective imaginary, moving beyond the binary of catastrophe and technological salvation.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian

articles.excerpt: Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey, opens at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. The show combines art, data, and research to examine community prosperity.
articles.content: Marking Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. Running from September 26, 2026, to January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation. The project is the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the university's Institute for Social Research. Developed in collaboration with researchers, data scientists, and students, the work examines forces shaping wealth and opportunity across income, education, housing, and business ownership. In other developments, Adriana Varejão is preparing to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia with a presentation curated by Diane Lima, placing her in conversation with artist Rosana Paulino. articles.title: Glenn Brown Collection Opens New Exhibition in London
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition Fail We May, Sail We Must has opened at the Brown Collection in London, bringing together works by more than twenty artists.
articles.content: The Brown Collection has launched the exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must, on view through August 7, 2027. Curated by Glenn Brown and collection cofounder Edgar Laguinia, the presentation features historic and contemporary paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists. The selection highlights how art spanning six centuries can challenge the mind and forge new connections between works not typically seen together, including pieces by Brown himself. In parallel developments, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly is now available alongside a new catalogue dedicated to Brice Marden. Additionally, artist Adriana Varejão is preparing a series of new paintings and sculptures to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, her exhibition titled Comigo ninguém pode places her in dialogue with Rosana Paulino to reflect on colonial history and the rewriting of the past within the Brazilian Pavilion's Modernist structure.

articles.originalTitle: Switzerland’s Fondation Beyeler opens £109.7m expansion - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler in Basel Opens Its £109.7m Expansion
articles.excerpt: The Fondation Beyeler in Basel has expanded its exhibition space with three new structures designed by architect Peter Zumthor and extended parklands.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Basel, Switzerland, is opening its extensive expansion project built at a cost of around SFr 120m. Known for its Modern art collection, the museum has added three new structures designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, alongside extended parklands. The principal Wyss building, named after Swiss entrepreneur Hansjörg Wyss who covered most of the cost, increases exhibition space by 1,500 sq. m. Additional structures include the freestanding Ammann Pavilion for recitals and performances, and the Erlen Torhaus office addition. The surrounding parkland has doubled to nearly 20,000 sq. m, featuring newly installed works by artists such as Rachel Whiteread, Pierre Huyghe, and Louise Bourgeois. To optimise visitor processes, the museum has planned a measured inauguration period from 26 September through 14 January, during which visitor numbers to paying exhibitions will be restricted.

articles.originalTitle: Turner Prize 2026 opens in North Yorkshire at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Turner Prize 2026 Exhibition Opens at Middlesbrough Institute
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Turner Prize exhibition has opened to the public at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art in northern England.
articles.content: The latest Turner Prize exhibition has opened to the public at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art in northeast England. Shortlisted artists Tanoa Sasraku, Marguerite Humeau, Simeon Barclay, and Kira Freije are featured following their solo exhibitions from the past year. The selected artists engage with subjects such as ecological thought, human precarity, oil geopolitics, and the experience of deindustrialisation. Sasraku explores extractivism through immersive settings, while Humeau creates sculptural compositions from materials including beeswax and ancient wood. Barclay presents an architectural intervention exploring masculine identity and class, and Freije exhibits fragile figurative sculptures made from steel and aluminium. According to Tate Britain director Alex Farquharson, the works represent a cross-section of visual arts in Britain today. The winner will be announced on 10 December during a ceremony at the institute, receiving £25,000, while runners-up will be awarded £10,000 each.

articles.originalTitle: The astonishing story of Van Gogh collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller is finally celebrated in an exhibition at Switzerland’s Kunstmuseum Basel - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Art Collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller's Life Celebrated at Kunstmuseum Basel
articles.excerpt: Kunstmuseum Basel is hosting an exhibition celebrating the life and pioneering art collecting of Gertrud Dübi-Müller, who purchased a Van Gogh portrait as a teenager in 1908.
articles.content: The life and collecting journey of Swiss pioneer Gertrud Dübi-Müller are the focus of an exhibition at the Kunstmuseum Basel. Inheriting wealth from her family's engineering business after being orphaned at a young age, Müller acquired Vincent van Gogh's Portrait of Charles-Elzéard Trabuc in 1908 when she was only 19 years old. This purchase predated widespread international recognition for the artist and sparked considerable enthusiasm among her avant-garde circle, including artists Cuno Amiet and Giovanni Giacometti. Alongside her early art acquisitions, Müller led an adventurous life, becoming the first woman in Solothurn to own a car. She later married lawyer Otto Dübi in 1921 and maintained her dedication to modern art throughout her life. Upon her death in 1980, Dübi-Müller bequeathed 190 works to the Kunstmuseum Solothurn, including pieces by Paul Cezanne, Henri Matisse, and Pablo Picasso alongside works by her Swiss artist friends. The exhibition runs until 7 February 2027, highlighting her remarkable early acquisition and her enduring engagement with modern art.

articles.originalTitle: Why Toronto is fast becoming unmissable for art - artbasel.com
articles.title: Toronto Arts Scene Expands Amid Diversity and Infrastructure Growth
articles.excerpt: Toronto is gaining prominence in the art world through its immigrant population and hybrid cultural fabric. Biennials, new art trails, and independent spaces strengthen the city's infrastructure, while commercial and studio space needs shape ongoing developments.
articles.content: Kenneth Montague, founder of The Wedge Collection, notes that Toronto's hybrid identity and multicultural fabric form the foundation of Canadian art. With 51 percent of its population born abroad, the city hosts a dynamic scene featuring artists showcased at international platforms like the Venice Biennale. Running its fourth edition this current month, the Toronto Biennial centers on the shared geographies of the Great Lakes and Indigenous artists to foster global dialogue. Along the waterfront, the Lassonde Art Trail—backed by 25 million dollars in seed funding from Pierre Lassonde—features 17 new commissions winding through Biidaasige Park. While curators and directors highlight the civic impact of these urban revitalization projects, artists point out that commercial infrastructure remains critical for the ecosystem. Artist-run spaces and newly established downtown studio initiatives maintain a grassroots momentum, while institutions like the Art Gallery of Ontario and MOCA expand their programming and gallery footprints. Local participants observe that while Toronto's collector base holds significant potential, the demand for affordable studio spaces and institutional growth continues as the local arts community navigates rapid urban development.

articles.originalTitle: Major Retrospective of Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa Opens at the Vitra Design Museum - Architectural Record
articles.title: Vitra Design Museum Opens Major Retrospective of Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa
articles.excerpt: The Vitra Design Museum in Germany is hosting a major retrospective examining the five-decade career of Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa through more than 250 works.
articles.content: The Vitra Design Museum in Weil am Rhein, Germany, is hosting a major retrospective dedicated to Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa. Titled 'Geoffrey Bawa: Architecture for the Senses', the exhibition runs from September 26 through February 28, 2027, and examines the architect's five-decade career through more than 250 drawings, models, photographs, furniture pieces, and archival documents. Marking the first major retrospective of Bawa in over 20 years, the exhibition is organized by the Vitra Design Museum, M+, and the Wüstenrot Foundation in collaboration with the Geoffrey Bawa Trust. The display features materials from projects such as the Bentota Beach Hotel, Kandalama Hotel, and his country estate Lunuganga, alongside newly commissioned photographs by Iwan Baan. The exhibition explores Bawa's integration of landscape and architecture, as well as his collaborations with Sri Lankan artists and craftspeople. Lebanese architect Lina Ghotmeh designed the scenography to create an immersive environment. Following its run in Germany, the exhibition will travel to M+ in Hong Kong in June 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Herzog & de Meuron reuses foundations for mass-timber Massachusetts school building - Dezeen
articles.title: Herzog & de Meuron Reuses Existing Foundations for Massachusetts College Building
articles.excerpt: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised existing concrete foundations for a new Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College, incorporating mass-timber levels and deep solar-shading eaves.
articles.content: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised the existing concrete foundation of an older structure for the Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College in Massachusetts, expanding the building from 80,000 to 120,000 square feet. Working alongside executive architect Sasaki, the studio preserved two lower-level foundations of the former Merrill Science Center to navigate the sloped site and align with the institution's carbon neutrality goals. Two upper levels constructed primarily from Canadian Black Spruce mass timber were added atop the skeleton, featuring light-oiled Western Red Cedar cladding above and dark-stained timber on the lower levels. The structural design connects mass-timber columns directly to pre-existing concrete supports using split-beam and corbel joints. The third level accommodates study and event spaces alongside a winter garden courtyard, while the roof holds low-lying pavilions containing a black-box theatre and solar panel arrays. According to the studio, the design achieves a 33 per cent reduction in embodied carbon and a 93 per cent reduction in operational carbon compared to conventional building types. This project marks Herzog & de Meuron's first completed educational building in the United States.

articles.originalTitle: Architectural Details: Snider House Bridges Past and Present - Architizer
articles.title: Giannone Petricone Associates Revitalizes 1828 Snider House in North Toronto
articles.excerpt: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and updated Snider House, North Toronto's oldest surviving building, blending historic design with a glass addition.
articles.content: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and revitalized Snider House, identified as the oldest surviving building in North Toronto. Originally built in 1828 in the Regency style, the landmark was upgraded to modern standards while preserving its historic character. The original Regency cottage façade maintains its formal, symmetrical presence at the front, while a contemporary rear glass extension opens the dwelling to the landscape. Co-founding principal Pina Petricone notes that the firm approaches heritage projects to celebrate distinct attributes through contrast and layering. The standout architectural feature at the rear is an undulating, two-story glass façade. Fabricated using a gravity-curved method on hot sand beds in Spain and combined with low-E insulated glass technology, this custom curtain wall contrasts with the heavy clay brick of the original structure. Inside, the restored interior balances heritage formality with material restraint, maintaining warmth in the dining and sitting rooms. The kitchen and adjoining living areas open fully to the backyard. Reimagined wide baseboards function simultaneously as visual accents and air diffusers, helping the historic home meet contemporary standards.

articles.originalTitle: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor - ArchDaily
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged park, and restored historic structures.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings designed by Peter Zumthor, an enlarged park, and adaptive reuse of historic structures. Extending the existing museum by Renzo Piano, the project introduces exhibition, educational, and public spaces while opening private landscape areas to visitors. The expanded ensemble opens on September 26, 2026, during a preview phase before a full opening on January 15, 2027. Zumthor's additions comprise the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus. The three-storey Wyss Museum adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space, featuring a Y-shaped plan arranged around existing trees and constructed using locally quarried Jura limestone. The single-storey glass and oak Ammann Pavilion functions as a public lounge and event space. The timber-frame Erlen Torhaus contains artwork handling facilities and workspaces. Landscape integration adds nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland, nearly doubling Beyeler Park's size. Restored historic structures include the Orangerie, Ammann Atelier, the Salon listening lounge, and the Folly experimental space. An inaugural exhibition titled 'Constellations' will bring together over 200 works from the collection and private loans across the venues from September 26, 2026, through September 5, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires Exhibition Opens at the V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum explores 1,600 years of artistic production across two empires in a major upcoming exhibition.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites visitors to explore 1,600 years of artistic production with the exhibition 'Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires', opening on 7 November 2026. Spanning from AD 330 to 1922, the exhibition brings together over 200 objects to examine the distinct yet connected traditions of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. Hosted at V&A South Kensington, the showcase highlights the creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond. The exhibition features four main sections: Grand Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. Across these sections, visitors can view rarely seen decorative arts, including fine silks, historic garments, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The curation traces changes in patronage, imperial spectacle, religious coexistence, and urban life, concluding with the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century Europe.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collections and Designs Unveiled at Paris Design Week 2026
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week gathered 500 exhibitors across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond. Designers and studios showcased contemporary collections rooted in craftsmanship, traditional techniques, and natural forms.
articles.content: Paris Design Week took place with the participation of 500 exhibitors across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and surrounding districts. The event featured contemporary creations rooted in traditional techniques, natural forms, and curated craftsmanship. Modern Metier presented Tropic of Capricorn, its second collection created with French designer Rudy Guénaire. Draga & Aurel showcased their Crisalide side tables at Galerie BSL, combining colored glass layers with sand-cast brass bases. Pinto partnered with Nobilis to introduce the Foundation collection, while Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection led by artistic director Tamara Taichman. Swedish design house Veermakers opened its inaugural Paris showroom in Le Marais. Nordic Knots presented wool rugs inspired by the Swedish Grace movement, and L'Objet collaborated with jeweler Jessica McCormack on a marine-themed home collection. Garnier & Linker introduced Aurora, its first outdoor lighting series in cast aluminum and alabaster. Franck Genser exhibited new iterations of his Decorative Arts-inspired designs, and Hervet Manufacturier presented its first full range of living and dining furniture.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sansetsukon and Es Devlin to Present Live Performance at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon will present MILK, a live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists, for free at the V&A East Storehouse on 3 October 2026.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is preparing to stage MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists. The event will take place on 3 October 2026 at Gallery 2 within the V&A East Storehouse. Scheduled for 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM, and 8:00 PM, each performance lasts between 25 and 30 minutes and is free to the public. Through dance, sound, light, and shadow, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and concepts regarding humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by artists. Performers move through the gallery to a soundscape created by reworking audio elements from The Everythingists. The ensemble features dancers Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, Robbie Ordoña, Peter Butler, Tania Dimbelolo, Lois Samphier, and Anna Watanabe, with a musical composition by Serian Griffiths and sound design by Nana Nakashima.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches 200,000 Members and Launches Landmark Open Call
articles.excerpt: Tate Collective, the free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached 200,000 members and launched an open call for a new artwork to be displayed at Tate Modern.
articles.content: Tate Collective, a free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached a milestone of 200,000 members. To mark the occasion, an open call has been launched inviting members to create a new artwork for display at Tate Modern alongside figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. The winning commission will be selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal and will go on display in March 2027, with submissions closing on 19 October. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having drawn 870,000 attendees over the past decade to after-hours events featuring live music, performances, and workshops. Karin Hindsbo, Interim Director of Tate, stated that the members represent a generation choosing to engage with art and ideas. The anniversary celebrations will culminate on 30 October with a special Late event programmed by Shygirl. Tate Collective membership offers various discounts and access to creative opportunities with support from patrons and foundations.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 Press Dossier: a deep-dive into this year's highlights - artbasel.com
articles.title: Art Basel Paris 2026 Opens With 211 Galleries and Expanded Programme
articles.excerpt: Hosting 211 galleries from 41 countries, Art Basel Paris 2026 begins on October 20 with an expanded public programme around the Grand Palais.
articles.content: Art Basel Paris brings together art professionals from 41 countries and regions with the participation of 211 galleries. The event features 183 galleries in the Galeries sector, alongside 16 in Emergence and 12 in Premise. This year, 32 participants join the fair for the first time, while more than 170 galleries return. The Premise sector moves to a larger space in Salon Seine, and the Conversations series relocates to the Grand Palais Auditorium. Sixty-four galleries operating in France play a central role, with galleries such as Petrine from Paris and Düsseldorf, and The Pill from Istanbul and Paris, graduating from Emergence to the Galeries sector. Established French galleries including Templon, Chantal Crousel, Perrotin, and Almine Rech are joined by international participants such as Gagosian, Hauser & Wirth, and David Zwirner. The preview, Avant-Première, returns on October 20. Highlighting the Parisian scene, presentations featuring works by figures such as Pol Taburet, Julien Creuzet, and Annie Ernaux combine disciplines including painting, installation, performance, literature, and moving image.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Large-Scale Robert Rauschenberg Display
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of over 20 works by Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades to mark the centenary of his birth.
articles.content: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of works by Robert Rauschenberg, running from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Marking the centenary of the artist's birth, the presentation brings together over 20 works spanning three decades, including paintings, prints, and kinetic installations. At the heart of the presentation are Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to the Tate Americas Foundation. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the display foregrounds Rauschenberg's engagement with dance and performance, featuring metal sculptures, performance sets, and costume designs. The exhibition is organized as part of the ARTIST ROOMS touring programme, jointly managed by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With Paris Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel marks its 90th anniversary with a dedicated exhibition opening at La Galerie du 19M.
articles.content:
Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition celebrating the journey from raw material to finished product. Part of Chanel's specialized workshop network since 1997, the house presents the display at La Galerie du 19M, Chanel's craftsmanship hub in northern Paris. Running from Sept. 23 until Dec. 13, the exhibition highlights ancient tools, techniques, and the work behind the designs.

Titled "Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel," the showcase begins with tree trunks carved into raw hat shapes alongside 4,000 wooden hat blocks from the archives. Curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer and Palais Galliera fashion museum director Emilie Hammen, the exhibition features specially commissioned artworks and runway designs. Maison Michel remains one of the few remaining producers mastering sewn straw, utilizing ancient sewing machines. The display explores headgear's evolution from social signifier to a form of personal expression, featuring items crafted from canvas, organza, leather, and tweed.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: Jacquemus Filled His New Miami Design District Flagship With Art — and Fine Design - WWD
articles.title: Jacquemus Opens New Flagship Boutique in Miami Design District
articles.excerpt: Paris-based fashion house Jacquemus is opening a two-story flagship boutique in the Miami Design District. Conceived by the founder, the 2,900-square-foot space incorporates blue-chip artworks, antiques, and bespoke design pieces.
articles.content: Paris-based fashion house Jacquemus is launching a 2,900-square-foot flagship boutique in Miami's Design District, spanning two floors. Conceived by founder Simon Porte Jacquemus in collaboration with architectural firm Oma, the interior echoes elements from earlier boutiques in Paris and Courchevel. The space integrates artworks by Germaine Richier, Aristide Maillol, Joan Miró, and Pablo Picasso, alongside furnishings by Frank Lloyd Wright and Jean Royère. Chief executive officer Sarah Benady described Miami as a natural convergence point for fashion, art, and design between the United States and Latin America. The boutique includes a dedicated shoe salon, a private VIC sunroom, and infrastructure prepared for an upcoming beauty line through a partnership with L'Oréal. Additionally, the location will offer an exclusive powder and mint blue edition of the Nike Moon Shoe. This opening follows recent retail expansions in New York and Los Angeles as part of the brand's targeted international retail strategy.
